title: The Edge Where Entropy Learns to Listen

features.name: the listening antenna
features.desc-on-touch: It was built to broadcast, but it learned instead to hear. The signal it transmits now is the landscape's own voice, encoded into wavelengths.

features.name: the chaos that learned manners
features.desc-on-touch: Entropy used to look like noise. Here, it learned to look like pattern. The chaos is still there—it just knows when to pause and listen now.

features.name: the border where broadcast ends
features.desc-on-touch: Beyond this point, the signal becomes weather. The archive chose to stop here because the country had learned to speak for itself.

features.name: the decoder that listens backward
features.desc-on-touch: It takes the landscape's incoherent data stream and learns meaning from it. Every storm, every wind, every bird call becomes legible here.

inscription: the broadcast stops here; beyond it, the country has learned to be its own archive

file.name: Dispersal_Signal_Final_Transmission.log
file.note: The last archival broadcast, followed by a recording of pure landscape data: wind patterns, bird calls, water flow. The archive learned to be silent so the country could speak.

exits.label: back toward the signal, back toward broadcast
deeper into the country that speaks in weather
toward the point where silence becomes listening
